description: A tool a workflow installs with `go install module@vN` is a pinned dependency that NO manager reads. Renovate's gomod manager looks at go.mod; github-actions looks at `uses:`; a version inside a `run:` block is seen by neither, so it is a pin that will never be offered an update.

Added on 2026-11-15, measured on this organisation rather than argued. `.github/workflows/vulns.yml` is the shared govulncheck lane that TEN modules of this org call, and it pins two tools inside one `run:` block: govulncheck@v1.9.0 and github.com/go-fleettools/fleettools/cmd/vulngate@v0.85.0. The Dependency Dashboard of this repository listed, for that file, exactly two dependencies -- actions/checkout and actions/setup-go -- and NEITHER of the `go install` pins. vulngate was at v0.85.0 while v0.123.0 was released: thirty-eight releases, with nothing watching.

⛔ And it is the worst possible place for an unread pin: vulngate is the JUDGE of every vulnerability finding in this organisation. A judge going quietly stale does not fail; it keeps answering, with an older idea of what counts.

depName is the MODULE, not the package: `go install` takes a package path and the proxy knows modules. The `/cmd/<name>` group is OPTIONAL because not every tool in this fleet lives at `<module>/cmd/<name>` -- go-fleettools/prwait and staletools have their main package at the module ROOT, and `go install github.com/go-fleettools/prwait@v0.10.0` is how they are installed. A module whose own path ends in `/cmd/<something>` would still be read wrong; none does here.

A version of `latest` is deliberately NOT matched: there is no version to compare or rewrite. An @latest in these lanes is a deliberate float, and the rule that should refuse an UNDECLARED one is go-fleettools/fleettools#289, not this manager.

⛔ NOT WRITTEN HERE FIRST. go-fleettools/.github and go-crdt/.github already carried this manager, with this reasoning; this is the third copy and the omission in this org is what left the pins above unwatched. Two copies of a rule is one copy being wrong, and the alternative -- a shared preset repository -- is a dependency every organisation's Renovate run must fetch before it can read its own config. Kept as copies deliberately, and every copy's description says so.

One pull request per repository for everything non-breaking, rather than one per dependency. Merging them singly means every merge rebases the others and restarts their checks: one run over an organisation of 34 repositories updated 109 branches and merged 2. Grouped, a repository needs one round of checks instead of dozens.

Never auto-merge the Go toolchain, and never let it ride in somebody else's group. A rule that says automerge:false for one dependency is defeated by grouping, because Renovate decides automerge per BRANCH: go 1.27.0 rode into seven repositories inside a branch called renovate/github-actions, whose other dependency was actions/setup-go. Ungrouped, it gets a branch of its own and this setting governs it. It matters because go1.27.0 miscompiles on loong64 (golang/go#81000, bisected on real hardware to 3fdac6780b): go-gfx/gfx fails that lane and stayed open only because the lane failed, which is the CI gate holding rather than this rule. A repository without such a lane sees nothing.
